title: ÖSTERREICHISCHE PHOTOVOLTAIK-STRATEGIE
description:
The "Österreichische Photovoltaik-Strategie" (Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy) is Austria’s official national strategy and policy framework for the coordinated expansion and promotion of photovoltaic (solar PV) energy generation. This comprehensive initiative includes a strategic action plan, serving as both a guideline and operational document, to achieve Austria's ambitious energy transition and climate policy targets by 2040. The strategy outlines clear national objectives, milestones, and measurable goals, detailing both sectoral and cross-sectoral expansion rates necessary to meet the targeted contribution of solar photovoltaics within Austria’s overall renewables and electricity mix.

Central to the strategy is the development and integration of robust regulatory, financial, and spatial planning measures designed to accelerate the deployment and market development of photovoltaic systems. It encompasses targeted efforts to expand PV capacity, modernize grid integration, foster supportive legal frameworks, and cultivate a favorable environment for ongoing technological innovation. In addition to scaling up installation rates, the strategy emphasizes the importance of research, industrial development, and workforce growth, aligning with both European and national aspirations for renewable energy leadership and technological advancement.

The "Österreichische Photovoltaik-Strategie" also promotes initiatives to enhance acceptance of solar PV within Austrian society and to facilitate the circular economy, aiming for efficient production, sustainable resource use, and end-of-life management of photovoltaic materials. It coordinates planning and implementation efforts at governmental and societal levels, addressing technical, ecological, social, and economic dimensions to ensure broad-based support and successful integration of photovoltaics throughout the nation.

By providing a comprehensive set of action fields and measures—spanning policy reforms, market incentives, infrastructure upgrades, research funding, and public engagement—the strategy serves as Austria’s blueprint for accelerating photovoltaic adoption and supporting the country’s transition towards a sustainable, low-carbon energy future through 2040.

title: BUNDESMINISTERIUM FÜR KLIMASCHUTZ, UMWELT, ENERGIE, MOBILITÄT, INNOVATION UND TECHNOLOGIE
description: The "Bundesministerium für Klimaschutz, Umwelt, Energie, Mobilität, Innovation und Technologie" (BMK), also known as the Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology of Austria, is the central governmental authority responsible for shaping and implementing Austria’s policies in a wide range of areas. These include climate protection, environmental conservation, energy policy, mobility and transport, as well as the promotion of innovation and technological advancement. The BMK is tasked with developing and executing national strategies aimed at climate action, such as expanding the use of renewable energy sources, particularly photovoltaics. Additionally, the ministry is responsible for authoring, publishing, and implementing comprehensive strategies and policies to further Austria’s climate, energy, and innovation objectives. Through its efforts, the BMK plays a crucial role in guiding Austria towards a sustainable, environmentally friendly, and technologically advanced future.

title: HUBERT FECHNER
description: Author of the strategy document; involved in photovoltaic strategy development and possibly an expert in the field, contributing to the national expansion process.

title: LEONORE GEWESSLER
description: The Federal Minister of Austria for Climate Action and the environment, serving as the public political face of the strategy; provides political leadership and vision for the energy transition and photovoltaic expansion.

title: ÖSTERREICH
description:
Österreich, also known as Austria, is a Central European nation and a member of the European Union that is at the forefront of renewable energy advancement, particularly in the field of photovoltaics (PV). The country has established comprehensive national strategies and regional initiatives focused on transitioning its energy system towards climate neutrality, with clear targets to fully shift its electricity generation to renewable sources by 2030 and achieve total energy independence from fossil fuels by 2040. Austria’s energy transition efforts prioritize the expansion and integration of photovoltaic installations, supported by significant public backing, robust governmental regulations, and substantial industrial participation.

Austria plays a leading role in the redevelopment of the European photovoltaic industry, contributing actively to the PV value chain through research, manufacturing, and employment, and fostering the innovation ecosystem in this sector. The country provides financial incentives, education, and support for innovation, thereby strengthening Europe’s renewable energy independence and resilience. National strategies emphasize not only the deployment of PV systems but also tackle challenges related to grid integration by advancing storage and flexibility solutions, thus ensuring the reliability and sustainability of the energy supply.

Key stakeholders in Austria’s PV and energy transition efforts include the government, industry, and the general public, all of whom show strong commitment to environmentally friendly, low-risk energy production, energy sovereignty, and economic value creation. Austria leverages its strengths in technology sectors such as electro-electronics, semiconductors, glass and metal processing, digitalization, and software to support its leadership in renewable energy. The country also participates in numerous collaborative European initiatives aimed at promoting industrial sustainability and accelerating the energy transition across the continent.

Österreich seeks to boost opportunities in research, strengthen its position as a hub for innovative companies in the PV industry, and expand its role within European PV value chains. Its coordinated strategies and long-term vision are designed not only to decarbonize the national energy system, but also to promote Austria as a model for renewable energy integration and a driver of the broader European energy transition.

title: WIEN
description: WIEN is the German name for Vienna, the capital city of Austria. It serves as the central hub for numerous governmental, educational, and organizational activities. Vienna is the location of the headquarters of the Ministry for Climate Action (BMK), and is frequently referenced in official documents as a point of publication and significant activity. In addition to housing the Ministry, Vienna hosts a number of universities and many other referenced organizations central to Austria’s cultural, administrative, and academic landscape. As the capital, Vienna plays a key role in national governance and is a focal point for both domestic and international affairs.

title: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-GESETZ (EAG)
description: The ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-GESETZ (EAG), known in English as the Federal Act on the Expansion of Renewable Energy or the Renewable Energy Expansion Act, is an Austrian legislative framework implemented from January 2022. This act aims to ensure that Austria's electricity demand is covered entirely by renewable energy sources by 2030, making it a cornerstone of the country’s photovoltaic and broader renewable energy strategy. The EAG provides a range of measures to promote the expansion and innovation of renewable energy installations. These include incentives and surcharges designed to support the development of innovative renewable energy technologies, as well as specific deductions for certain types of photovoltaic installations. By establishing these financial mechanisms and legal targets, the EAG serves as a crucial driver in Austria’s transition towards a sustainable, renewable-based energy sector.

title: INTEGRIERTER ÖSTERREICHISCHER NETZINFRASTRUKTURPLAN (ÖNIP)
description: The Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan, which assessed the photovoltaic expansion potential of 41 TWh by 2040 and guides national planning and infrastructure development.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK (PV)
description: The technological process of converting solar energy into electricity; central to Austria's renewable energy and climate neutrality targets and highlighted as a strategic pillar in the national energy transition.

title: CAJETAN PERWEIN
description: Cajetan Perwein is credited as a photographer for the foreword section of the Österreichische Photovoltaik-Strategie document for the Austrian Ministry for Climate Action.

title: BMK
description:
BMK, the commonly used abbreviation for the Austrian Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology (Bundesministerium für Klimaschutz, Umwelt, Energie, Mobilität, Innovation und Technologie), is a central governmental body in Austria responsible for shaping and implementing national strategies in climate action, environment, energy, mobility, innovation, and technology. The ministry holds a significant role in the formulation, coordination, and execution of Austria’s energy and climate policies, including the development and publication of major strategic documents such as the national photovoltaic strategy. BMK leads the transformation of Austria's energy and transport systems by designing and allocating financial instruments and resources aimed at advancing renewable energy, enhancing energy efficiency, and supporting sustainable mobility.

A key responsibility of BMK is the organization of stakeholder dialogues and roundtables to analyze and address challenges, such as those related to integrating renewable power plants into the national grid. The ministry works actively in monitoring and guiding energy technology markets and plays a strategic role in policy creation, ensuring that market development in segments like photovoltaics aligns with Austria’s overarching climate and energy targets. BMK is also involved in supporting and facilitating just transition initiatives, which aim to ensure that the shift towards a low-carbon economy is inclusive and equitable. This work is reinforced by the ministry’s financial programs, which provide funding and incentives to drive sustainable innovation and technological advancements.

Moreover, BMK's mandate includes the design of educational efforts and awareness campaigns to foster societal engagement in the energy transition, thereby supporting Austria’s goals for climate neutrality. Through its comprehensive approach, BMK ensures that the transformation of both the energy and transport sectors is underpinned by robust policy, stakeholder consensus, and the necessary financial support. The ministry’s multifaceted activities are frequently covered in recent market reports, underscoring its pivotal role in Austria’s transition to a sustainable, climate-resilient future.

title: EU-ERNEUERBAREN-RICHTLINIE (RED III)
description: The EU Renewable Energy Directive (RED III) is a European Union legal framework that came into effect on November 20, 2023. It sets binding targets for all EU member states to increase the share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption, raising the minimum target to 42.5% by 2030, with the aspiration of reaching 45%.

title: EUROPA
description: EUROPA (Europe) is the continent where Austria is located and serves as the broader regional context for developments in the fields of photovoltaics (PV) and energy policy. Within this framework, Europe is characterized by the integration of national power markets, the implementation of European quality norms, and a commitment to advancing renewable energy sources. European Union directives guide the member countries, including Austria, towards achieving energy independence by promoting collective efforts for increased adoption of renewable energies, such as photovoltaics. This continental approach ensures that energy policies, market integration, and quality standards are harmonized across Europe, supporting Austria’s PV strategy while contributing to the overall advancement of sustainable energy solutions within the region.

title: KLIMA- UND ENERGIEFONDS
description:
The **KLIMA- UND ENERGIEFONDS** (Climate and Energy Fund) is an Austrian governmental and public organization dedicated to advancing climate protection, supporting energy transition, and promoting energy autonomy across Austria. As a national funding body, it provides substantial financial resources and initiates strategic programs to support the expansion of renewable energy technologies, including photovoltaic (PV) systems, energy storage, and other clean energy solutions.

The fund plays a crucial role in facilitating Austria’s progress toward sustainability by supporting a wide range of projects, studies, and strategies that focus on climate action, renewable energy deployment, and innovative energy solutions. Notably, in 2023, the Klima- und Energiefonds inaugurated new programs aimed at accelerating the expansion of PV installations and promoting advanced energy storage infrastructure, reflecting Austria’s commitment to a robust and resilient green energy sector.

Additionally, the Climate and Energy Fund is instrumental in fostering the development of energy communities—local groups or regions empowered to generate, share, and manage renewable energy collectively. Through dedicated support mechanisms and financial incentives, the fund enables these communities to pursue greater energy autonomy and local climate solutions.

Moreover, the Klima- und Energiefonds actively implements initiatives such as the Green Finance Support Program, which is designed to stimulate sustainable investments and encourage the integration of green finance principles throughout Austria’s energy and climate-related markets. By blending direct project funding with strategic support for broader innovation and policy development, the fund serves as a cornerstone for Austria’s transition to a low-carbon, sustainable energy future.

In summary, the KLIMA- UND ENERGIEFONDS is a comprehensive Austrian national body committed to financing and guiding projects, strategies, and innovative programs that promote renewable energy, energy efficiency, climate protection, and sustainable development. Through its various programs and initiatives, it plays a pivotal role in Austria’s ongoing energy transition and climate action efforts.

title: ENERGIEWENDE
description:
The "Energiewende" in Austria refers to the national energy transition, a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming the country's energy, electricity, and heating systems. The primary goal of this transition is the complete decarbonization of Austria’s energy sector and the exclusive use of renewable energy sources, with the target of achieving climate neutrality by 2040. This ambitious movement includes a broad range of concerted actions, policies, and strategies at both the national and European Union levels, all focused on reducing dependence on fossil fuels and promoting sustainability.

A key aspect of the Austrian Energiewende is the widespread adoption of renewable energy technologies, particularly solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, as well as a significant emphasis on community participation and energy independence. The process seeks to decarbonize the electricity system with a specific target of reaching 100% renewable electricity generation nationwide by 2030. To accomplish these objectives, Austria is investing in the research and development of innovative, climate-friendly energy technologies and components, thereby reinforcing its position as a hub for technology competence and innovation.

Furthermore, the Energiewende serves as an umbrella term for the broad set of policies, societal changes, events, and technological advancements required to shift the entire energy system away from fossil fuels towards renewable sources. This national initiative not only focuses on technical transformation but also includes community engagement, strengthening local and national capabilities, and ensuring sustainable and secure energy supply for future generations.

Overall, the Energiewende in Austria embodies a holistic transformation of the entire energy landscape, combining strong policy frameworks, research efforts, technological innovation, and active societal involvement to ensure climate neutrality and enhanced energy security by 2040.

title: KLIMANEUTRALITÄT 2040
description: KLIMANEUTRALITÄT 2040, or Climate Neutrality 2040, is Austria’s official political objective to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by the year 2040. This ambitious target means that, by 2040, Austria aims for its energy system and all related sectors to no longer contribute to net greenhouse gas emissions, effectively reaching climate neutrality. The goal serves as a foundational milestone that shapes national policy across various domains, including technology development and educational initiatives, and is especially central to the country’s photovoltaic (PV) development strategy. By striving for Klimaneutralität 2040, Austria is committed to transforming its energy landscape and economy in order to actively combat climate change and fulfill its environmental responsibilities at both national and international levels.

title: PV-STRATEGIE
description: The photovoltaic strategy is a coordinated plan developed by Austria for the expansion of photovoltaics, including actions, goals, and implementation steps to support the country's transition to renewable energy.

title: KLIMABONUS
description: Klimabonus is a financial bonus program by the Austrian government that provides compensation to households as a part of carbon pricing policy.

title: ÖKOSTROMANLAGEN
description: Ökostromanlagen refers to "green electricity plants" supported and incentivized under Austrian renewable energy laws such as the EAG.

title: LAND
description: The Land refers to the provincial or state-level governments within Austria, playing a significant role in implementing frameworks, regulations, and infrastructure for the energy transition and PV expansion.

title: GEMEINDE
description: Gemeinde refers to local or municipal governments in Austria, actively involved in the planning and realization of PV projects and energy infrastructure at the community level.

title: E-CONTROL
description:
E-CONTROL is the official Austrian regulatory authority tasked with overseeing and managing the country's electricity and gas markets. As the central organization responsible for the regulation and monitoring of Austria’s energy systems, E-CONTROL ensures the reliability, transparency, and fairness of energy supply throughout the nation. Their responsibilities include the publication and implementation of regulatory action plans, such as the “Aktionsplan Netzanschluss,” which are designed to facilitate major national objectives, including the integration of renewable energy sources.

E-CONTROL plays a leading role in supporting Austria’s energy transition, particularly by advancing initiatives and solutions that promote the adoption and integration of renewables—most notably photovoltaics (solar energy). The authority undertakes and publishes grid flexibility studies, supports network connection initiatives for new energy sources, and is actively engaged in developing strategies—such as the comprehensive action plan issued in July 2023—to ensure that the nation's grid infrastructure can accommodate the growing share of renewable electricity.

In addition to its technical and strategic functions, E-CONTROL is cited in various referenced reports as a source of expertise and regulatory guidance on energy market oversight, market liberalization, and the maintenance of a secure and competitive energy environment. The organization also plays a key role in shaping policy implementation related to both operational energy supply security and the acceleration of renewable energy technologies, with a particular focus on supporting the national photovoltaic strategy.

Overall, E-CONTROL serves as Austria's principal authority for the regulation, supervision, and modernization of the electricity and gas sectors, with an integral role in the country's ongoing energy transformation and commitment to sustainable energy solutions.

title: WISSENSCHAFT
description: WISSENSCHAFT refers to Austria’s scientific community, including universities, research institutes, and other scientific organizations. The Wissenschaftssektor is actively involved in the development and assessment of new technologies, particularly in the field of the energy transition (Energiewende). These institutions play a pivotal role in both researching and implementing scientifically sound measures that support Austria’s shift towards sustainable energy. Specifically, WISSENSCHAFT contributes to the advancement and adoption of photovoltaic technologies and strategies, utilizing academic expertise and scientific methodology to guide innovation and practical application. Through this collaborative effort, Austria’s scientific sector ensures that energy transition measures are evidence-based and effective, thereby playing a crucial role in shaping the country’s future energy landscape.

title: WIRTSCHAFT
description: WIRTSCHAFT refers to Austria's economic and business sector, encompassing a wide range of companies and industries, including the photovoltaic (PV) industry. This sector is significantly impacted by ongoing changes such as the energy transition, which shapes both challenges and opportunities. The Wirtschaftssektor is not only affected by these transformations but also stands to benefit through innovation and growth, particularly as companies embrace new technologies and adapt to market demands. Within the context of Austria, WIRTSCHAFT plays a proactive role in driving advancements related to the energy transition by engaging in PV project implementation and supporting the broader adoption of renewable energy solutions. The sector demonstrates a commitment to collaboration, particularly in initiatives aimed at securing qualified professionals—a critical need to sustain growth and maintain competitiveness. By fostering innovation and investing in workforce development, Austria’s WIRTSCHAFT positions itself to enhance the country’s competitiveness in both national and international markets, especially within the PV sector. Overall, the economic and business sector in Austria is characterized by its adaptability, collaborative spirit, and dedication to technological progress amidst the challenges of the energy transition.

title: INTERESSENSVERTRETUNGEN
description: INTERESSENSVERTRETUNGEN are advocacy and interest groups in Austria, including organizations such as industry associations, stakeholder organizations, unions, and NGOs. They play a significant role in representing the interests of various parties involved in the implementation of photovoltaic (PV) technology and broader energy system changes. These groups actively contribute the perspectives and concerns of different societal segments to the energy policy decision-making process, ensuring that a diverse range of viewpoints and needs are considered. By participating in policy discussions, INTERESSENSVERTRETUNGEN help shape energy policy outcomes, promote stakeholder engagement, and support the integration of innovative energy solutions within the Austrian energy sector.

title: INTEGRIERTER ÖSTERREICHISCHER NETZINFRASTRUKTURPLAN (NIP)
description:
The INTEGRIERTER ÖSTERREICHISCHER NETZINFRASTRUKTURPLAN (NIP), or Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan, is a central and strategic planning document that provides a comprehensive framework for the development and expansion of Austria's energy network infrastructure. Serving as both a guideline and a planning authority, the NIP assesses and plans for the nation's energy grid needs, covering both electricity and gas networks. This crucial document plays a key role in aligning infrastructure development with Austria’s national energy targets and timelines.

The NIP identifies potential sites and infrastructure required for the integration and deployment of renewable energy sources across the country, such as photovoltaic installations, and includes projections for their expansion up to the year 2040. It analyzes various scenarios and assesses the potentials for expanding not only the electricity grid but also the broader energy network to support the transition to renewable energy. By mapping out possible developments and required actions, the NIP ensures that network expansion remains synchronized with Austria’s long-term goals for increasing the share of renewable energy in its energy mix.

Furthermore, the NIP serves as a foundational resource for policymakers, regulators, and industry stakeholders by providing detailed projections, site assessments, and coordination of network development measures. This integrated approach helps Austria to efficiently plan, invest in, and implement the necessary infrastructure changes to achieve climate and energy objectives, thereby supporting the country’s commitment to a sustainable and secure energy future.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK-STRATEGIE
description: Die österreichische Photovoltaik-Strategie ist ein umfassendes, anpassbares Planungs- und Steuerungsdokument, das Ziele, Maßnahmen und Effekte für den Ausbau der Photovoltaik bis 2040 beschreibt und regelt.

title: EU-EMISSIONSHANDEL
description: Der EU-Emissionshandel ist das zentrale europäische Instrument zur Bepreisung und Reduktion von CO₂-Emissionen für besonders energieintensive Sektoren.

title: EUROPÄISCHE UNION
description: The EUROPÄISCHE UNION (European Union, EU) is a political and economic union currently comprising 27 member states across Europe. It functions as a Staatenverbund (association of states) whose legal frameworks and research programs have a significant impact on the implementation of climate and energy transition policies in member countries, such as Austria. The EU sets binding, overarching targets related to renewable energy development, nature conservation, and energy efficiency for all its members. In this context, it establishes legislative and regulatory instruments—including directives like RED III (Renewable Energy Directive III) and supporting laws such as the Nature Restoration Law—which guide national policies and legislation. Through these measures, the EU plays a central role in shaping the climate, energy, and environmental strategies within its territory, ensuring coordinated progress towards sustainability and climate neutrality among its member states.

title: FORSCHUNGSRAMMENPROGRAMM
description: Das Europäische Forschungsrahmenprogramm ist das umfassende EU-Programm für Forschung und Innovation, das als Leitbild für die Entwicklung des österreichischen Wirtschaftsstandortes dient.

title: LANDESREGIERUNGEN
description: Österreichische Landesregierungen sind für die Umsetzung der Energiewende und die Beteiligung an bundeslandspezifischen Maßnahmen zuständig.

title: GEMEINDEN
description: Österreichische Gemeinden spielen eine Schlüsselrolle bei der Umsetzung erneuerbarer Energien und der Transformation auf lokaler Ebene.

title: NETZBETREIBER
description: Netzbetreiber sind für den Betrieb, Ausbau und die Zuverlässigkeit des Stromnetzes in Österreich zuständig, insbesondere im Zuge des Ausbaus erneuerbarer Energien.

title: ELEKTROTECHNISCHE NORMUNGSORGANISATION
description: Elektrotechnische Normungsorganisationen legen technische Standards für den sicheren Ausbau und Betrieb von PV-Anlagen und anderen energietechnischen Einrichtungen fest.

title: STROMMARKT
description: Der Strommarkt bezeichnet den Handelsplatz für elektrische Energie, an dem durch die Energiewende neue Rollen für Bürger:innen als aktive Marktteilnehmer entstehen.

title: REGIERUNGSPROGRAMM
description: Das Regierungsprogramm umfasst die politischen Zielvorgaben und Maßnahmen der Bundesregierungen in Österreich für Klimaschutz, Energiewende und Innovation.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK-AUSBAU
description: Der Ausbau der Photovoltaik in Österreich ist ein laufender Prozess mit dem Ziel, bis 2040 einen maßgeblichen Anteil der Energieversorgung durch Sonnenenergie zu erzielen.

title: BUNDESLÄNDER
description: The "Bundesländer" are the federal states within Austria, functioning as subnational administrative regions. Each Bundesland is responsible for setting and implementing ambitious targets for the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure, including photovoltaic systems. They play a central role in Austria's renewable energy strategies, holding primary jurisdiction over areas such as building and spatial planning, and nature conservation. Additionally, the Bundesländer are integral in supporting regional aspects of energy strategy; this includes aiding energy communities by providing advisory centers and implementation support. Collectively, the Bundesländer are crucial to achieving Austria's renewable energy objectives, working both independently and collaboratively to meet national and regional targets for sustainable energy development.

title: PV-ANLAGE
description: PV-ANLAGE (Photovoltaic system) refers to decentralized solar power generation installations that are widely deployed in Austria for electricity production across buildings and infrastructure. Collectively, PV-ANLAGE encompasses various types of photovoltaic (PV) installations or plants, which play an essential role in the renewable electricity production sector of Austria. Photovoltaic installations under PV-ANLAGE include a range of system types such as rooftop systems, building-integrated photovoltaics, freestanding solar plants, and community PV systems. These installations are designed to generate solar energy primarily for local consumption, but they are also capable of storing energy and exporting surplus electricity to the grid. By contributing clean, renewable energy, PV-ANLAGE supports Austria’s efforts in advancing sustainable energy solutions and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

title: BIOENERGIE
description: BIOENERGIE refers to the sector in Austria dedicated to the generation and use of renewable energy derived from biological sources, such as biomass. This sector plays a key role in Austria’s overall renewable energy supply, harnessing various organic materials—including agricultural byproducts, wood, and other biological matter—to produce energy. The use of bioenergy not only supports Austria’s efforts to diversify its energy portfolio and increase sustainability, but also complements other renewable energy sources within the country. As an integral component of Austria’s renewable energy strategy, BIOENERGIE contributes to reducing dependence on fossil fuels and lowering greenhouse gas emissions, thereby supporting environmental and climate goals.

title: WASSERKRAFT
description: WASSERKRAFT, also known as hydropower, is a renewable energy source that significantly contributes to Austria's electricity generation. Representing hydropower generation facilities and operations, WASSERKRAFT plays a major role in the country's renewable electricity sector, highlighting its importance in Austria's overall energy mix.

title: WINDENERGIE
description: WINDENERGIE refers to the wind energy sector in Austria, which is a significant contributor to the country’s renewable electricity supply. As a vital component of Austria’s national renewable energy mix, WINDENERGIE plays an important role in advancing sustainable energy production and supporting Austria's goals for cleaner, greener power generation.

title: GRÜNER WASSERSTOFF
description: Grüner Wasserstoff, or green hydrogen, refers to hydrogen produced by using renewable electricity, such as that generated from solar power and other renewable energy sources. In Austria, grüner Wasserstoff is specifically produced via renewable methods, including solar energy, making it a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional hydrogen production techniques. This form of hydrogen serves as an energy carrier, enabling the storage of surplus electricity generated from photovoltaic (PV) systems and other renewable sources. Additionally, grüner Wasserstoff is intended for both storage and export, helping to stabilize the energy supply and offering opportunities for Austria to utilize or share excess renewable energy resources.

title: ENERGIEGEMEINSCHAFTEN
description:
ENERGIEGEMEINSCHAFTEN (energy communities) are formal or informal organizations or associations composed of citizens, companies, or localities that collaborate to generate, share, and use renewable energy, with a particular focus on photovoltaic (PV) power. Functioning primarily at the local or community level, these groups enable members to jointly produce, store, and consume electricity, often through the integration of PV and storage solutions within neighborhoods or districts.

In Austria, Energiegemeinschaften are legally enabled entities that support the decentralized production and use of renewable energy, such as solar power. They allow residents and companies to participate in the collective development, management, and utilization of renewable energy projects, thereby encouraging local engagement and promoting energy autonomy. By facilitating joint action, these communities not only contribute to value creation for their members but also play a crucial role in Austria’s transition toward decentralized power systems and the broader expansion of community-driven PV installations.

Overall, Energiegemeinschaften serve as a key driver for sustainable energy practices, empowering various stakeholders to take an active role in the energy transition and reinforcing community-level participation in renewable energy generation, storage, and consumption.

title: FREIFLÄCHEN-BIODIVERSITÄTSANLAGEN
description: FREIFLÄCHEN-BIODIVERSITÄTSANLAGEN are large-scale, ground-mounted photovoltaic (PV) parks located in Austria. These installations are purposefully designed not only for the generation of electricity but also to foster biodiversity and support ecological restoration. By integrating solar energy production with the simultaneous creation and preservation of natural habitats, Freiflächen-Biodiversitätsanlagen contribute to habitat diversity. Their dual function ensures that the implementation of renewable energy infrastructure goes hand-in-hand with ecological enhancements, making them a pioneering approach to sustainable land use in the context of Austria’s transition to renewable energy sources.

title: AGRI-PV-ANLAGEN
description:
AGRI-PV-ANLAGEN are agricultural photovoltaic installations, also known as agrivoltaic systems, that integrate solar energy generation with active agricultural activities on the same land area. These systems are designed to enable simultaneous farming and electricity production by installing photovoltaic panels within agricultural fields or on farmland. By combining the dual use of land for both crop cultivation or livestock grazing and solar power generation, AGRI-PV-ANLAGEN help enhance land-use efficiency and support the economic resilience of farms through diversified income streams.

In Austria, AGRI-PV-ANLAGEN are promoted in line with the country's renewable energy expansion laws, which provide subsidies for agrivoltaic projects as long as the agricultural productivity of the land is only minimally affected. This legislative framework encourages the adoption of photovoltaic technology within agricultural landscapes while ensuring that farming remains a principal activity. The goal is to maintain high standards of agricultural output alongside renewable electricity generation, contributing to sustainable rural development and the broader transition toward clean energy.

Overall, AGRI-PV-ANLAGEN represent an innovative approach to land management that aligns with both environmental and economic objectives. By integrating photovoltaic systems with agricultural operations, these installations help farmers increase their income, support the expansion of renewable energy, and optimize the use of available land resources.

title: SOLARINDUSTRIE
description: SOLARINDUSTRIE, referring to the solar power industry in Austria and across Europe, encompasses a broad spectrum of activities including research, manufacturing, deployment, and export of solar technologies. Within Austria, the solar industry (Solarindustrie) is composed of manufacturers, exporters, and technology developers specializing in photovoltaic (PV) technologies. This industry plays a significant role in advancing innovation and maintaining international competitiveness, both by developing cutting-edge solar solutions and by engaging in the export of technologies to global markets. Through its focus on research and development, manufacturing excellence, and export activities, SOLARINDUSTRIE is a key contributor to the growth of renewable energy in Austria and throughout Europe.

title: PV-WERTSCHÖPFUNGSKETTE
description: The PV-WERTSCHÖPFUNGSKETTE, also known as the PV value chain, encompasses all stages of innovation, production, and deployment within Austria’s photovoltaic sector. This value chain includes a comprehensive range of activities, starting from the initial stages of research and technological innovation, progressing through the manufacturing of photovoltaic (PV) technology, followed by its deployment and installation. Additionally, the PV-WERTSCHÖPFUNGSKETTE covers the end-of-life processes of PV technology, such as recycling, ensuring that the full lifecycle of photovoltaic products is addressed within Austria’s solar energy industry.

title: BIODIVERSITÄTS-SOLARPARKS
description: Biodiversitäts-Solarparks are specialized solar parks designed not only for electricity generation but also to provide significant ecological benefits. These solar parks are intentionally developed to foster biodiversity and support the restoration of natural habitats, creating environments that promote the presence and flourishing of a variety of plant and animal species. By integrating renewable energy production with ecological enhancements, Biodiversitäts-Solarparks offer a dual function: delivering clean electricity while supporting the conservation and restoration of local ecosystems.

title: FACHKRÄFTE
description: "FACHKRÄFTE" refers to highly qualified and skilled professionals, specialists, and workers who possess technical or vocational expertise within the photovoltaic (PV) and broader renewable energy sector in Austria. These individuals play essential roles in the installation, manufacturing, and operation of PV technology. The term encompasses both those currently active in the industry and those targeted for continued development and retention in order to support Austria's PV industry. FACHKRÄFTE are central to advancing the adoption and maintenance of PV technologies and ensuring the continued growth and innovation within the Austrian renewable energy sector.

title: HANDWERKSBETRIEBE
description:
HANDWERKSBETRIEBE are artisan and craft enterprises that play a crucial role in Austria's renewable energy landscape, particularly within the photovoltaic (PV) sector. As skilled craft and trade businesses, Handwerksbetriebe offer a wide range of services including the installation, maintenance, and technological support for PV systems and related technologies. They are characterized by their expert knowledge and practical experience, ensuring reliable and high-quality execution of technical tasks critical for the deployment and ongoing operation of solar energy systems.

In response to the growing emphasis on sustainable energy, Handwerksbetriebe have increasingly positioned themselves as innovative contributors to the renewable energy market in Austria. Their adaptability and skill set allow them to capitalize on the expanding opportunities within the PV sector. These enterprises not only install and maintain PV systems, but often take an active role in integrating new technological advancements and optimizing system performance, thereby driving forward the transition to cleaner energy sources.

In summary, Handwerksbetriebe are key players in Austria’s move toward renewable energy, providing indispensable expertise and practical services for PV systems while continually adopting innovations to meet the evolving demands of the sector.

title: AKTIVER KUNDE
description: AKTIVER KUNDE (“Active Customer”) refers to a legal or natural person, as defined under Article 15 of EU Directive 2019/944, who is entitled to participate directly in electricity markets. The term primarily applies to residents or consumers who actively engage in the production, self-consumption, and management of electricity—most commonly through personal or shared photovoltaic (PV) installations. An Aktiver Kunde not only produces and consumes their own electricity, often serving as a prosumer, but may also share electricity with others within a community or participate in collective PV initiatives. Through these activities, active customers can influence market dynamics and grid stability, either individually or as part of a broader energy community. Overall, an Aktiver Kunde plays a significant role in the evolving energy landscape by contributing to decentralized energy production, enhancing renewable energy uptake, and supporting the effective functioning of both local and broader electricity networks.

title: GEBÄUDEAUSSENTEILE
description: Building exteriors (Gebäudeaußenteile) in Austria are now commonly used for weather protection as well as for integrated PV power generation.

title: UMWELTBUNDESAMT
description: Umweltbundesamt is Austria's Environment Agency. It provides scientific and analytical support, prepares scenarios for greenhouse gases and energy, and informs policy, including the "Transition 2040" scenario noted in the context of PV expansion projections.

title: EUROPÄISCHES PARLAMENT UND RAT
description: The European Parliament and Council ("Europäisches Parlament und Rat") are legislative institutions of the European Union, responsible for setting EU directives, including the 2019/944 regulation on rules for the internal electricity market referenced in the text.

title: P. BIERMAYR
description: P. Biermayr is an author and recognized research or academic expert who has made significant contributions to the analysis of Austria's photovoltaic (PV) market. As a lead or co-author, P. Biermayr was instrumental in producing the "Innovative Energietechnologien in Österreich, Marktentwicklung 2023" report, which was published in 2024 for the BMK (Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology). This comprehensive report serves as a key source of market data and analysis for the Austrian PV sector, providing critical insights into the development and trends of innovative energy technologies in Austria. Biermayr’s expertise and leadership in the field are demonstrated through the depth of analysis and authoritative data presented in the report, making him a significant figure in Austria's ongoing energy transition efforts.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIKANLAGEN
description: Photovoltaikanlagen (Photovoltaic Installations) refers collectively to all organizations, firms, and actors involved in the deployment, operation, ownership, management, and expansion of photovoltaic systems for electricity generation in Austria. These photovoltaic installations, commonly known as photovoltaic systems, play a central role in harnessing solar energy to produce solar electricity. The term encompasses a broad range of entities, including organizations and operators that are directly responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining the systems, as well as the entities focused on expanding the reach and efficiency of photovoltaic energy across Austria. As a whole, Photovoltaikanlagen contributes significantly to Austria’s efforts in sustainable electricity generation and the national transition towards renewable energy sources.

title: MEHRFAMILIENHÄUSER
description: Mehrfamilienhäuser, or multi-family buildings, refers here to residential organizations or legal entities whose residents are now able to participate in PV generation and community energy initiatives.

title: TRANSITION 2040
description: Transition 2040 is a climate and energy scenario provided by Umweltbundesamt, projecting the trajectory of Austria's electricity system and greenhouse gas emissions up to 2040, informing policy and infrastructure plans.

title: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-GESETZ
description: The Austrian Renewable Expansion Act ("Erneuerbaren-Ausbau-Gesetz", EAG) is a law regulating and promoting the growth of renewable energies, including PV, setting specific targets and subsidy frameworks.

title: STROMNETZ
description: The public electricity grid (Stromnetz) in Austria is the infrastructure network that distributes electricity, crucial for connecting PV installations and ensuring electricity delivery to consumers nationwide.

title: TEILNEHMER:INNEN MEHRFAMILIENHÄUSER
description: Residents of multi-family buildings (Teilnehmer:innen Mehrfamilienhäuser) in Austria who are participants in the energy transition by utilizing PV and energy community models.

title: BETREIBER:INNEN DER PV-ANLAGEN
description: Operators or owners of PV installations (Betreiber:innen der PV-Anlagen) are individuals or companies who directly operate photovoltaic systems, participating in energy markets.

title: BÜRGER:INNEN
description: BÜRGER:INNEN refers to Austrian citizens who are recognized as central stakeholders and beneficiaries in the country’s energy transition, particularly within the context of decentralized energy generation and energy communities. These citizens are not only the end-users of energy but are also increasingly viewed as direct beneficiaries of innovative energy community and participation models, notably in the photovoltaic (PV) sector. Through evolving strategies and incentives, BÜRGER:INNEN are being encouraged and empowered to take a more active role in the energy sector, fostering broader participation in renewable energy projects and energy markets. As such, they are being positioned as both active participants and key drivers in Austria’s shift toward more sustainable and community-oriented energy solutions. By participating in energy communities and decentralized generation initiatives, citizens contribute directly to the success of the PV energy transition and the broader aims of renewable energy adoption across Austria.

title: UNTERNEHMEN
description: UNTERNEHMEN refers to companies (corporate entities) operating in Austria, encompassing both large corporations and small businesses. These companies are notable for integrating smart energy management systems and photovoltaic (PV) installations into their daily operations and overall energy usage. The term generally applies to businesses that are actively engaged in advanced and sustainable practices, particularly in the fields of sustainability, energy, and financial markets. Austrian Unternehmen are distinguished by their commitment to optimizing energy efficiency and embracing renewable energy solutions, reflecting a broader trend toward sustainable development and innovation within the Austrian business sector.

title: FORSCHUNGSEINRICHTUNGEN
description: Research institutions (Forschungseinrichtungen) in Austria leading the advancement of PV and renewable energy-related technologies and innovation.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK
description: PHOTOVOLTAIK refers to the deployment and expansion of photovoltaic (PV) technology in Austria, which is recognized as a key milestone and ongoing process in the country’s pursuit of climate neutrality. The strategic growth of PV systems is regarded as a central component in achieving Austria's energy transition objectives. It not only enables the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions but also boosts the nation’s energy sovereignty by increasing the share of domestically produced renewable energy. Furthermore, the expansion of photovoltaic technologies supports a wide array of economic, technological, and social sectors. It contributes to sustainable economic development by fostering job creation, stimulating technological innovation, and securing Austria's leadership role in renewable energy. Socially, the proliferation of PV systems encourages public participation in the energy transition, enhances local resilience, and promotes sustainable practices across communities. Overall, PHOTOVOLTAIK plays a crucial role in Austria's efforts to meet its climate targets and support the broader transition to a sustainable energy future.

title: WOHNUNGSEIGENTUMSGESETZ
description: The Wohnungseigentumsgesetz (Housing Property Act or Austrian Home Ownership Act) is a piece of legislation in Austria that governs property ownership, particularly in the context of apartments, row houses, and individual buildings. In January 2022, the Wohnungseigentumsgesetz was amended to introduce significant simplifications for the construction of photovoltaic (solar) installations. These changes were specifically designed to make it easier for property owners in terraced houses (row houses) and detached (single) buildings to install photovoltaic systems. The amendments aim to promote sustainable energy solutions by reducing bureaucratic obstacles and streamlining the approval process for such installations, thereby supporting Austria's climate and energy goals.

title: ELEKTRIZITÄTSWIRTSCHAFTSGESETZ
description: The Electricity Management Act, a legislative package in Austria under review in early 2024, intended to further regulate and promote the expansion and management of the electrical power industry, especially concerning photovoltaics.

title: INNOVATIVE UNTERNEHMEN
description: Austrian innovative companies that operate in the photovoltaic sector, driving technological advances, industrial production, and economic value creation within the country.

title: ÖSTERREICHISCHE WIRTSCHAFT
description: The Austrian economy, which benefits from the expansion of photovoltaics through increased value creation, lower and more reliable electricity prices, and a strengthened business location.

title: BEVÖLKERUNG
description: The population of Austria, regarded as an active participant in the energy transition and beneficiary of increased energy sovereignty and affordable energy due to expanded photovoltaic use.

title: PRODUZENT:INNEN
description: Producers (manufacturers) in Austria’s photovoltaic industry, including internationally operating specialists, contributing to domestic value creation and employment.

title: PV-INDUSTRIE
description: PV-INDUSTRIE refers to the photovoltaic industry sector in Austria, which includes a wide array of businesses, companies, and organizations engaged in the industrial-scale manufacturing, deployment, research, and maintenance of photovoltaic systems. This sector encompasses all activities involved in the production of photovoltaic components and systems, the delivery and installation of solar technology, as well as ongoing operational support. PV-INDUSTRIE represents the collective efforts of Austrian manufacturers, service providers, and research institutions dedicated to advancing and expanding photovoltaic technology throughout the country.

title: GEWERBE
description: Commercial trades and businesses working alongside the PV industry, providing skilled employment and supporting the sector’s growth in Austria.

title: PRIVATPERSONEN
description: Private individuals in Austria who are targeted by policy incentives to install photovoltaic systems and thus play a pivotal role in decentralized energy production.

title: ELEKTRIZITÄTSWIRTSCHAFTSGESETZ (ELWG)
description:
The Elektrizitätswirtschaftsgesetz (ELWG), also known as the Austrian Electricity Industry Act, is a newly established and recently updated legislative framework governing the Austrian electricity industry. As of early 2024, the ElWG is under review and introduces a comprehensive set of contemporary regulations designed to address the evolving challenges facing the electricity sector. Central to its purpose is the facilitation of grid connection for renewable energy plants, including photovoltaic systems, reflecting Austria's commitment to expanding the role of renewables in its energy mix.

The ELWG sets out clear rules and requirements for the management and operation of the electricity grid, with a focus on promoting the integration of renewable energy sources. To this end, the Act introduces measures that enhance market transparency, create new roles within the electricity market, and provide increased flexibility, all aimed at accelerating the deployment of renewable energy systems. The legislation is intended to support the faster and more efficient integration of renewables by removing barriers to grid access and establishing a supportive regulatory environment.

Overall, the Elektrizitätswirtschaftsgesetz (ELWG) positions Austria’s electricity industry for a sustainable future by modernizing its legal framework, streamlining the integration of renewable energy technologies, and fostering a transparent, flexible, and innovation-friendly electricity market.

title: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-BESCHLEUNIGUNGSGESETZ (E-ABG)
description: The Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act is in preparation to accelerate procedures for the establishment of photovoltaic systems and the necessary infrastructures for the energy transition.

title: BUND
description: The federal government of Austria, which collaborates with the states (Bundesländer) to achieve national renewable energy and electricity consumption goals.

title: BUND-LÄNDER-DIALOG ERNEUERBARE ENERGIE
description: A cooperation committee between the federal government (Bund) and the federal states (Bundesländer) aiming to reach national targets for renewable energy through joint strategy development and ongoing evaluation.

title: LANDESENERGIEREFERENT:INNEN
description: Regional energy ministers or representatives from the Austrian states involved in the decision to establish the Bund-Länder-Dialog for Renewable Energy.

title: EU
description:
The European Union (EU) is a political and economic union composed primarily of European countries. It plays a central role in shaping regulations, laws, and strategies aimed at promoting sustainable energy production, driving the energy transition, and fostering competitive industries across its member states. The EU is known for orchestrating comprehensive policy initiatives, such as the Net Zero Industry Act and the EU-Taxonomy, which are designed to boost clean technology production and provide financial support to sustainable industries. Notably, the EU provides guidance, funding, and strategic support to individual member states—such as Austria—to facilitate their green transformation efforts.

In addition to engineering collaborative efforts among its members, the EU establishes directives and renaturation goals with significant impacts on national policies concerning energy performance, conservation, and the expansion of renewable energy sources. These directives ensure that member states align with broader environmental, economic, and sustainability objectives set forth by the union. Through these multifaceted actions, the European Union continues to be a key orchestrator of Europe’s collective response to climate change, industrial competitiveness, and the advancement of a sustainable, low-carbon future for its members.

title: KLIMAMODELLREGIONEN
description: Designated climate model regions in Austria intended to be advanced as leading regions for ambitious PV generation and ecological practices.

title: LANDWIRTSCHAFT
description: The agricultural sector, identified as a key player for implementing and benefiting from Agri-PV systems which enable dual land use and increased efficiency.

title: ENERGY PERFORMANCE OF BUILDINGS DIRECTIVE
description: A legal directive of the European Union, as of April 12, 2024, requiring certain energy performance standards (including PV mandates) for buildings.

title: PV-ANLAGEN
description: PV-ANLAGEN refers to the deployment, installation, expansion, and operation of photovoltaic (solar) installations in Austria. These PV systems are a central component of Austria's transition to renewable energy, known as the Energiewende. The integration of photovoltaic installations is considered a significant event within the transformation of Austria's renewables sector, highlighting their essential role in increasing renewable energy production across the country. By harnessing solar power, PV-ANLAGEN contribute substantially to Austria’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions and achieving a more sustainable energy future.

title: PV-FREIFLÄCHENANLAGEN
description: The implementation of large-scale ground-mounted photovoltaic systems, including regulations and incentives for such installations.

title: PV-DACHGÄRTEN
description: A strategy or event referring to the construction of photovoltaic rooftop gardens aimed at ecological benefits and urban greening in Austria.

title: GRÜNDACH
description: The implementation of green roofs, sometimes in combination with PV for mutually reinforcing environmental and energy benefits.

title: NATUR
description: Natural landscapes and environments which are to be protected and integrated into renewable energy planning in Austria.

title: RAUM
description: Represents spatial planning areas within Austria, crucial for renewable energy infrastructure and building developments.

title: GEBÄUDE
description: Buildings in Austria, subject to new or updated regulations for renewable energy integration, such as PV obligations on new construction and renovations.

title: PARKPLÄTZE
description: Parking areas within Austria being considered for mandatory photovoltaic installations to utilize already sealed surfaces for renewable energy.

title: VERTEILERNETZ
description: The distribution network for electricity in Austria, key to implementing transparency measures and facilitating grid access for new PV systems.

title: NETZENTWICKLUNGSPLÄNE
description: Publication and planning events where grid development plans are made available to guide Photovoltaic (PV) growth.

title: REIHENHÄUSER
description: Terraced houses in Austria, now benefiting from regulatory simplification for PV installation.

title: EINZELGEBÄUDE
description: Individual buildings in Austria, affected by new guidelines making it easier to mount PV systems.

title: NEUBAU
description: Construction of new buildings in Austria, increasingly subject to PV installation mandates.

title: SANIERUNG
description: Renovation events on buildings in Austria, which now often trigger solar/PV installation requirements.

title: BIODIVERSITÄT
description: The process or outcome of enhancing biodiversity, especially through PV design and land use, aligning with national and EU renaturation goals.

title: RENATURIERUNGSZIELE
description: EU-wide and national restoration goals aiming to enhance biodiversity and natural habitats, with which PV projects must align.

title: VERSIEGELTE FLÄCHEN
description: Already-sealed (e.g. paved, built-upon) surfaces in Austria, targeted for renewable energy installations to optimize existing land use.

title: FÖRDERMITTEL
description: The process/event of distributing funding or subsidies to promote the deployment and integration of PV and other renewable technologies.

title: EUROPAPARLAMENT
description: European Parliament, legislative body of the EU, passed resolutions supporting nature protection and renewable energy measures, including the Nature Restoration Law.

title: RED III
description: RED III, or the Renewable Energy Directive III, is a significant legislative act within the European Union, formally known as Directive (EU) 2023/2413. It amends several previous directives with the overarching goal of promoting the use of energy from renewable sources throughout the EU. Under RED III, member states are required to identify and define renewables acceleration areas—specific regions prioritized for renewable energy development. Additionally, the directive mandates that each member state must present strategic plans for advancing renewable energy initiatives, which includes setting and adhering to specific implementation deadlines. Through these measures, RED III seeks to accelerate the EU’s transition to renewable energy, ensuring coordinated and timely progress across all member states.

title: NATURE RESTORATION LAW
description: An EU law debated and supported by the European Parliament (as of July 2023) aimed at protecting and restoring nature and biodiversity within the EU.

title: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-BESCHLEUNIGUNGSGESETZ (EABG)
description: Austrian Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act (EABG) seeks to simplify and accelerate permitting and development of renewable energy facilities, including PV, within Austria.

title: ÖKODESIGN-RICHTLINIE
description: EU Ecodesign Directive, a regulatory framework for improving the environmental performance of products, now expanded to include a life-cycle approach and applies to the photovoltaic sector.

title: HACKNER, JOHANNES
description: Johannes Hackner is an individual recognized for his expertise in the field of renewable energy in Austria. He is identified as an author of the study "Anschluss erneuerbare Energien," which analyzes the challenges and requirements for grid connection of renewable energy facilities in Austria. In addition, Johannes Hackner is cited as an author or contributor to various expert documents and studies focusing on photovoltaic (PV) systems and renewable energy in Austria, demonstrating his involvement in the advancement and analysis of renewable energy integration and grid management within the country.

title: EPOOL
description: EPOOL is an Austrian organization actively engaged in renewable energy research, advocacy, and consultancy. The organization has been specifically referenced in connection with reports and studies concerning photovoltaic (PV) installation and the broader field of renewable energy within Austria. EPOOL has contributed to research on renewable energy grid connections, notably through its involvement in the study titled "Anschluss erneuerbare Energien." The group works closely with entities such as PV Austria, supporting the development, integration, and policy advancement of renewable energy solutions in the country. By participating in key studies and providing expertise, EPOOL plays a significant role in advancing Austria's renewable energy sector, particularly in the integration and connection of renewable sources such as solar PV to the national grid.

title: PV AUSTRIA
description: PV Austria is an organization dedicated to promoting the use and development of photovoltaics (solar energy) in Austria. As an association advocating for photovoltaics, PV Austria plays a significant role in advancing PV strategies and supporting the broader adoption of renewable energy solutions within the country. The organization actively participates in shaping energy policy and fostering sustainable energy initiatives. Furthermore, PV Austria is recognized as a co-author of key studies on the grid connection of renewable energy systems, demonstrating its expertise and leadership in technical and policy aspects of integrating photovoltaics into Austria's energy infrastructure. Through its advocacy, research, and involvement in industry advancements, PV Austria continues to contribute significantly to Austria's transition toward renewable, sustainable energy sources.

title: STAKEHOLDERRUNDEN DES BMK
description: Stakeholder rounds organized by BMK to discuss and address challenges in the grid connection and operation of renewable (especially PV) generation facilities.

title: INFRASTRUKTUREINRICHTUNGEN
description: Infrastructure facilities in Austria, including transportation, utility, and other structures evaluated for their potential to host renewable energy installations as identified in the Austrian NIP.

title: FREIFLÄCHEN
description: Open areas or free land in Austria considered as sites for the deployment of renewable energy systems, especially ground-mounted PV installations.

title: ERNNEUERBAREN-BESCHLEUNIGUNGSGEBIETE (RENEWABLES ACCELERATION AREAS)
description: Designated zones within EU member states, including Austria, where permitting and deployment of renewable energy systems can be expedited under RED III.

title: PRODUKTQUALITÄT
description: Product quality is a key element of the quality assurance measures promoted across the renewable/PV value chain; here it comprises organizations, certifications, and standards related to production, installation, repair, and service.

title: SERVICE
description: Service organizations are businesses or providers responsible for installation, ongoing maintenance, and potential repair work on photovoltaic installations.

title: REPARATUR
description: Repair organizations offer services for the maintenance and repair of PV equipment and infrastructure in Austria.

title: ENTSORGUNG
description: Waste management organizations involved in the responsible disposal, recycling, or repurposing of PV system components at the end of their lifecycle.

title: JOHANNES HACKNER
description: Johannes Hackner is an individual associated with the organization EPOOL and PV Austria and is an author or contributor to the study "Anschluss erneuerbare Energien".

title: AKTIONSPLAN NETZANSCHLUSS
description: The Aktionsplan Netzanschluss (Network Connection Action Plan) is a regulatory or policy initiative of E-Control for a seamless grid connection process for customer installations, notably those generating renewable electricity.

title: MUSTER- & LEUCHTTURMPROJEKTE PHOTOVOLTAIK
description: The Muster- & Leuchtturmprojekte Photovoltaik is a funding program of the Klima- und Energiefonds, supporting exemplary and flagship photovoltaic projects in Austria.

title: VERTEILNETZ
description: The distribution grid (Verteilnetz) is the local infrastructure network in Austria for distributing electricity, increasingly significant due to decentralized renewable and PV generation.

title: EUROPÄISCHER STROMMARKT
description: The European electricity market (europäischer Strommarkt) is the integrated power trading market in Europe, with which Austria interacts through market coupling and power export considerations.

title: BAU- UND LANDWIRTSCHAFT
description: The construction and agricultural sectors (“Bau- und Landwirtschaft”) in Austria, involved as key stakeholders and application areas for innovative integrated photovoltaic applications.

title: VERKEHRSSEKTOR
description: The transportation sector (“Verkehrssektor”) is a critical area in Austria for integrating photovoltaic applications, such as e-mobility and hydrogen production.

title: SMARTES LOKALES ENERGIEMANAGEMENT
description: Smart local energy management refers to the systems and processes that optimize the local generation, storage, and consumption of electricity, particularly from PV, in private households and companies.

title: WÄRMEPUMPE
description: The heat pump (Wärmepumpe) sector, referenced as a key technological component of Austria’s energy transition and the integration of decentralized renewable power.

title: WASSERSTOFF
description: The hydrogen (Wasserstoff) sector is an emerging technological field in Austria and Europe for energy storage, transformation, and as part of sector coupling strategies with renewables.

title: E-MOBILITÄT
description: E-mobility (E-Mobilität) is the electric vehicle sector, referenced as a key area for integration with solar energy and Austria’s energy transition strategy.

title: ERNEUERBARE ENERGIEN
description: Renewable energies (“erneuerbare Energien”) is the collection of organizations, technologies, and industries in Austria involved in producing energy from renewable sources, including solar PV.

title: KUND:INNENANLAGEN
description: Customer installations (Kund:innenanlagen) refer to private and commercial energy generation assets, such as rooftop PV systems, which require seamless grid connection solutions as referenced in Austrian regulation.

title: INDUSTRIELLE UND GEWERBLICHE PROZESSE
description: Industrial and commercial processes (“industriellen und gewerblichen Prozessen”) in Austria, mentioned as sectors where PV-generated power is to be utilized through load management and smart technologies.

title: EUROPÄISCHER MARKT
description: The European market refers to the interconnected electricity and energy markets across Europe, where generation and pricing trends—including those for PV energy—are coordinated and observed across member countries.

title: ANLAGENBETREIBER:INNEN
description: Anlagenbetreiber:innen (plant operators) include all persons or businesses responsible for operating photovoltaic installations in Austria, ensuring expansion and compliance with financial, legal, and technical frameworks.

title: ERGEBNISAUSBAU-GESETZ (EAG)
description: The Erneuerbaren-Ausbau-Gesetz (EAG) is Austria’s Renewable Energy Expansion Act, which establishes policies for market premiums and incentives promoting renewable energy projects, including PV.

title: EMOBILITÄT
description: E-Mobilität refers to the broad transition to electric mobility, including infrastructure and market initiatives for electric vehicles and their synergy with renewable electricity.

title: PV-RAHMENBEDINGUNGEN
description: PV-Rahmenbedingungen describes the regulatory and policy framework affecting the operation, support, and profitability of photovoltaic installations in Austria.

title: STROMNETZE
description: Stromnetze refers to the electricity grid operators in Austria who are responsible for integrating and managing electricity production and storage, including from PV."

title: GROSSSPEICHER
description: Großspeicher refers to companies or projects developing and managing large-scale electric energy storage systems—primarily for grid balancing and PV integration—in Austria.

title: WASSERSTOFF-ELEKTROLYSEURE
description: Wasserstoff-Elektrolyseure refers to organizations, equipment operators, and projects dedicated to producing hydrogen via electrolysis for long-term energy storage in Austria.

title: ANREIZE UND FÖRDERUNGEN
description: Anreize und Förderungen (incentives and subsidies) refer to ongoing national or regional programs or events that provide financial or regulatory support for PV expansion in Austria.

title: 13 AKTIONSPLAN NETZANSCHLUSS
description: The "13 Aktionsplan Netzanschluss" is an official Austrian action plan regarding grid connection policies published in July 2023 by E-Control.

title: AKTIONSPLAN NETZANSCHLUSS 2023
description: "AKTIONSPLAN NETZANSCHLUSS 2023" is a strategic action plan released in Austria in 2023 by E-Control, the country's energy regulatory authority. This comprehensive document serves as a detailed regulatory guide focused on facilitating the connection of renewable energy sources, with particular emphasis on photovoltaic installations, to the national electricity grid. The plan outlines clear procedures, regulations, and requirements for the seamless integration of these energy sources, aiming to support Austria's transition to sustainable energy and to enhance the efficiency and reliability of grid operations. By providing a structured framework for network integration, "AKTIONSPLAN NETZANSCHLUSS 2023" plays a key role in advancing Austria’s renewable energy objectives.

title: MARKTPRÄMIE
description: The "Marktprämie" (market premium) is a support instrument for PV operators, introduced via Austria’s EAG, to promote the profitability of renewables by compensating for market price differences.

title: UMSATZSTEUER-BEFRREIUNG 2024/2025
description: The VAT exemption for PV systems up to 35 kWp in 2024 and 2025 is a temporary fiscal measure in Austria to increase investment in solar power.

title: UMSATZSTEUER
description: Umsatzsteuer (value-added tax or VAT) pertains to taxation issues for photovoltaic operators, particularly the 2024/2025 exemption.

title: NOTSTROMSYSTEME
description: Notstromsysteme (emergency power systems) are systems and suppliers that ensure electricity to critical consumers during grid outages, referenced as part of resilience measures in Austria.

title: ERSATZSTROMSYSTEME
description: Ersatzstromsysteme (backup power systems) refer to organizational or technological solutions guaranteeing almost complete electricity supply for households or enterprises in case of power outage.

title: VERORDNUNGEN
description: Verordnungen (regulatory decrees) are legal instruments passed by government agencies, used to set subsidy amounts and adapt regulation for PV and storage in Austria.

title: RANDZEITEN
description: Randzeiten (fringe times) refer to edge periods—morning/evening or winter—when optimized PV systems can enhance yields.

title: WINTERZEITEN
description: Winterzeiten (winter times) signify the winter periods targeted by certain PV plant orientations in Austria.

title: STROMMARKTPREISE
description: Electricity market prices are dynamic prices on the Austrian and European energy markets, sometimes becoming very low or even negative during strong PV production.

title: BI-DIREKTIONALES LADEN
description: Bidirektionales Laden (bidirectional charging) describes the use of electric vehicles both for consumption and grid storage, referenced as an emerging business model and incentive target.

title: EABG
description: Abbreviation not explicitly defined in the text, but contextually the EABG is responsible for regulations and promotion of photovoltaic applications on infrastructures such as large parking lots, especially regarding their legal or technical facilitation.

title: BUNDESVERBAND NEUE ENERGIEWIRTSCHAFT (BNE) E.V.
description: BUNDESVERBAND NEUE ENERGIEWIRTSCHAFT (BNE) E.V. is a German-based association that plays a significant role in advancing new energy economies within Germany. Also known as the Federal Association of New Energy Industry (bne) e.V. or the German Federal Association for New Energy Economics (bne e.V.), the organization is recognized for its advocacy and expertise in the field of renewable energy economics. BNE e.V. is particularly noted for its contributions to best practices in the development of solar parks, especially emphasizing biodiversity-friendly approaches. The association conducts research, undertakes studies, and provides policy advice and guidelines aimed at integrating biodiversity conservation within the implementation of solar energy projects. By promoting the coexistence of solar infrastructure and ecological sustainability, BNE e.V. supports the transition towards environmentally responsible and economically viable renewable energy solutions in Germany. Its efforts are frequently referenced and serve as benchmarks within the industry for successfully aligning energy production with ecological best practices.

title: UNI KLAGENFURT
description: UNI KLAGENFURT, also known as the University of Klagenfurt, is an Austrian academic institution recognized for its active involvement in research related to renewable energies. The university engages in a wide range of energy research projects, with particular emphasis on the area of photovoltaics. In addition to its scientific research activities, UNI KLAGENFURT conducts annual studies assessing public opinion and attitudes toward renewable energy sources. These efforts contribute valuable data and insights into the advancement of renewable energy technologies and the understanding of societal perspectives on energy transition within Austria.

title: WU WIEN
description: Vienna University of Economics and Business (WU Wien) is an academic institution in Austria that conducts research on renewable energies and the social acceptance of these technologies. WU Wien actively contributes to reports and studies focused on renewable energy issues within Austria, providing important insights and analysis related to the country’s evolving energy landscape. Through its research activities, the university enhances understanding of both technical and societal aspects of renewable energy adoption, supporting Austria’s efforts towards sustainable energy solutions.

title: OEGUT
description: The Austrian Society for Environment and Technology (ÖGUT) is an organization that documents and disseminates best practices and methodological information regarding social innovation in the context of the energy transition.

title: AUSTRIAN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT ("BUND")
description: The Austrian Federal Government is the national governing body responsible for deploying photovoltaic systems on its buildings where technically and economically feasible.

title: PV-BIODIVERSITÄTSANLAGEN
